name: Bach
kurzbeschreibung: Charming village in the Lechtal valley, featuring traditional farms and stunning views of the Lechtaler Alpen.
beschreibung:
Overview

Bach im Lechtal is a charming alpine municipality in the Reutte district of Tyrol's Außerfern region, situated at around 1,070 meters above sea level in the upper Lech Valley. Home to approximately 650 residents, the municipality encompasses historic hamlets including Stockach, Schönau, Sulzlbach, and the remote mountain hamlet of Madau. Nestled between the rugged crags of the Lechtal Alps to the south and the Allgäu Alps to the north, Bach lies at the heart of the Nature Park Tiroler Lech, which protects one of Central Europe's last dynamic, untamed wild river ecosystems. The village is renowned for its grand heritage farmhouses adorned with elaborate Lüftlmalerei frescoes, while the local mountain Jöchelspitze serves as a premier year-round alpine destination.

History

Clearing and settlement of the upper valley began in the High Middle Ages by pioneers arriving from the Allgäu and Vorarlberg. Bach was first documented in 1427. Until roughly 1854, the municipality officially bore the name Stockach before Bach became the municipal denomination. For centuries, the community belonged to the Ehrenberg lordship within the Mitter-Lechtal district. Due to impoverished soils and bitter winters, many men from the 17th to 19th centuries migrated seasonally as skilled masons, stucco plasterers, and carpenters to Bavaria, Switzerland, and Alsace. The prosperity they brought back is reflected in the splendid murals and ornamental woodwork embellishing historic village facades. The Neoclassical parish church of the Purification of Mary was constructed between 1790 and 1792, while in the Madautal valley, the Baroque Holy Trinity Chapel erected in 1679 stands as a poignant reminder of alpine history following an avalanche disaster.

How to Get There

By car, motorists reach Bach from Reutte or Füssen along the Lechtal federal highway B198 in roughly forty minutes. During summer, a breathtaking scenic route leads from Innsbruck via Imst across the high Hahntennjoch pass road L72 to Elmen and onwards to Bach; in winter, when the pass is closed, access is via the Fernpass B179 and Reutte. From western Austria, the Hochtannberg Pass connects into the valley during summer months. Rail travelers take trains to Reutte in Tirol or Füssen station, connecting directly with hourly VVT regional bus line 110 into Bach.

Tips

Taking the modern 8-seater gondola of the Lechtaler Bergbahnen up to the Jöchelspitze at 1,800 meters unlocks panoramic alpine vistas across the river valley. Adjacent to the mountain station, the Lechtal Mountain Hay Museum illustrates the arduous labor of alpine haymakers in past centuries. Long-distance walkers treasure the certified Lechweg trail, which winds past pristine gravel banks between Holzgau, Bach, and Elbigenalp. Another natural wonder is the hike through the wild Sulzlbach Gorge with its carved rock tunnels to the traditional Sulzlalm hut. In the secluded hamlet of Madau, the rustic Berggasthof Hermine welcomes mountain enthusiasts. Winter delights guests with family skiing on Jöchelspitze and over one hundred kilometers of Nordic cross-country tracks along the river.
